data.headline: Hold 1 week of stock, then lift price 4% in week 4
data.why: Bean costs have already doubled and could double again; the simulation shows this plan adds the figures above in profit versus doing nothing, pays back by week 2, and never exceeds the $5,000 cash on hand. Half of customers prefer you over the rival, so a modest increase keeps volume while covering rising input costs.
data.watch_out: If bean prices spike a third time, unit cost jumps faster than the 4% price rise and margins compress; the bad case is selling at a loss while locked into 3 weeks of expensive inventory.
data.recheck_when: Re-check when the C-price breaks a new high or the next USDA crop report lands.

what_happened.text: The monthly arabica price peaked at its highest since 2011, after the 2021 frosts and dry weather in Brazil.
Frost worries in Brazil eased and arabica fell to a six-month low.
The World Bank's monthly arabica price was $5.64 a kg, against $5.91 in December 2021: within a few percent all along.

caveats: Coffee is about a quarter of a drink's cost in the owner's own words (milk, cups and syrups are the rest). A café buys roasted coffee, which follows the green bean price with a lag.
The series is the world arabica green bean price (Pink Sheet, monthly, $/kg). It is a 'nothing much happened' case: prices were already high and stayed high.
Each monthly value is treated as the month's mid-point, with straight lines between them.

The model has seen this period. Nemotron Ultra's model card gives a pre-training cutoff of September 2025 and a post-training cutoff of May 2026, so a date in the prompt cannot make it forget. The run only gives it news from before the date, and the leak check looks for hindsight in what it wrote.

“Best plan in hindsight” is the best of about 230 plans on a fixed grid (price, start, end, extra stock), run on the real path. Shoppers react to a sweep plan like they did to the nearest price plan the analysis tested; with none tested, they are neutral.
News pages are read as they are today. Any article that names a date after the as-of date is dropped, but a page edited later could still carry hindsight.

A plan that switches supplier is scored with the share of the price rise that Ultra assumed the alternative supplier would feel (`alt_shock_exposure`). The real price path says nothing about whether another supplier would really have been shielded, so those plans' results rest on that assumption.
